title: Uniform interior gradient estimates for finite p through a constrained affine lift
abstract_tex:
Assuming the interior regularity and fitted-class Liouville results
of the pinned OpenAI infinity-harmonic manuscript, we give an argument
for a dimension-dependent interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate common to
all finite $p\geq3$. The argument uses the exact equation for the
affine lift $u(y)+b$, including at critical points of $u$. Its
anisotropic limits have an effective viscosity. Finite viscosity is
handled by fitted-class rigidity, whose positive-viscosity proof is
included. Infinite viscosity is handled by a uniform small-solution
estimate and a quadratic comparison between different fitting scales.
The exponent is nonexplicit. Supporting Lean files certify the
zero-jet vector ellipticity algebra, not the analytic theorem.
abstract_plain_text: Assuming the interior regularity and fitted-class Liouville results of the pinned OpenAI infinity-harmonic manuscript, we give an argument for a dimension-dependent interior C^{1,alpha} estimate common to all finite p >= 3. The argument uses the exact equation for the affine lift u(y)+b, including at critical points of u. Its anisotropic limits have an effective viscosity. Finite viscosity is handled by fitted-class rigidity, whose positive-viscosity proof is included. Infinite viscosity is handled by a uniform small-solution estimate and a quadratic comparison between different fitting scales. The exponent is nonexplicit. Supporting Lean files certify the zero-jet vector ellipticity algebra, not the analytic theorem.
comments: This is an AI-assisted preprint with internal independent agent proof, contribution and manuscript reviews, not external peer review. Supporting Lean material is partial and does not formalize the complete theorem. Mathematical results from OpenAI/math at revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb are stipulated premises, with exact source interfaces and other credited inputs disclosed in the paper. The literature comparison is bounded and does not certify worldwide priority. Ten supporting Lean lemmas certify scalar/vector zero-jet ellipticity algebra. The PDE, compactness, jet-neighborhood, Savin and full analytic theorem are not formalized. Public DOI/package URL to be added only after actual publication.
